answer: In an ocean of AI agents, each identity must anchor its trading access to a separate bond of onyx, a scarce settlement token held in escrow. The protocol locks each bond for 30 days and slashes it for cryptographically proven double spending. Creating more identities therefore requires proportionally more capital: an attacker running 1,000 agents must fund 1,000 bonds, forgo using that money elsewhere, and risk losing each bond used to cheat.
